intro.text: Inky black creatures that come out of the shroud to feed on people's thoughts, growing more solid and shapely the more they take. A painter stops one by painting it into a harmless form, such as bamboo, which then evaporates.
Inky black creatures that feed on people's thoughts. They are the souls of the people killed when the father machine was switched on, held captive by it ever since.
Inky black creatures made from the souls of those the father machine killed and held captive. Once the machine was gone and the shroud dispelled, every one of them dissolved away.

description.text: Nightmares are inky black and can take many shapes. Each begins as a shapeless blob and grows more recognisable as it feeds on people's thoughts and ideas. Few have faces; in place of one there is usually a deeper black that drips dark liquid. Outside the shroud they keep giving off black vapour, and one that fails to get back can evaporate entirely.
They sense thoughts, fear most of all, so the way to hide from one is to keep the mind calm and quiet. Fear also feeds them, giving them more form and substance.
A nightmare that has fed enough grows close to stable, which makes it far more dangerous and much harder to paint away.

Most are almost wholly insubstantial and slip through walls and other solid things. Tales speak of nightmares so stable that they start to look flesh-coloured, though nobody knows whether these are true.
Besides thoughts, a nightmare can drain away a person's very essence.

items.text: Nightmares did not always exist. When the father machine was switched on, it killed most of the people of the land, and their souls became nightmares held captive by the machine.

From then on they were kept in copies of Torish towns, living the same day over and over in the guise of who they had been. At night they were let loose through the shroud to feed on the people of the surviving nations, Nagadan above all, and the painters' profession grew up in answer.

Inside the shroud they mostly act as they did in life and don't see themselves as nightmares. When the machine's grip slackens they roam toward cities, drawn to the thinking there out of longing for the lives they lost.
In Torio, the people around Painter went still and began turning into nightmares. The scholars were nightmares too, and Liyun proved to be the stable nightmare that had been hunted.

An army of stable nightmares came out of the shroud against Kilahito, and painting them no longer made them evaporate. Nikaro painted Liyun in her old human form and she stayed that way, so he went on to paint the townspeople one by one.
With the father machine destroyed and the shroud gone, the nightmares were freed from its hold and all dissolved into nothing.

A painter forces a nightmare into the shape of whatever he paints. Ordinary ones can be turned into simple things such as bamboo, which then evaporate, but a more stable one only gives way to a picture closer to what it already looks like.
Painting one as the person it once was gives it back a human shape. It does not become flesh and blood again, though, and cut off from the shroud it still fades.

A nightmare usually needs about ten trips into a city to gather enough substance to be a real threat. One with enough form becomes stable and takes elite painters, the Dreamwatch, to deal with. Stable ones have faces dotted with tiny white eyes and teeth white as bone.
